The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 02.09.2019 deceased Vasanthalakshmi had been moving on TVS Apache motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA53EZ7063 as pillion rider at about 9.00 a.m.
nearby Somayajalapall Village, Somayajalapalli Ramasamudram road Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District along with her nephew Sudindra, while going in high speed a dog came on the road, in order to avoid the dog in high speed rash and negligently,
rider of the motor cycle has suddenly applied brake, due to the impact of applying brake, motor cycle skid down, they fell down on the road, so that, deceased Vasanthalakshmi sustained SCCH 5 grievous injuries, hence she was immediately taken to Government Hospital Madanapalli of Chittur District, thereafter shifted to MVJ Hospital Hosakote, then shifted to Silicon City Hospital Hosakote, during treatment on next day 03.09.2019 at about 8.00 p.m. she succumbed to the said injuries.

sentences.text:
Then shifted to Government Hospital Hosakote, post mortem is conducted,
thereafter taken to their native place, conducted funeral ceremony, for medial expenses and funeral ceremony in all they have spent an amount of Rs.3,00,000/.

At the time of the accident, deceased Vasanthalakshmi was aged about 49 years, she was working as tailor and homemaker, earning Rs.25,000/ p.m., due to the sudden demise of Vasanthalakshmi,
petitioners being a husband and daughters of the deceased, suffered a lot physically, SCCH 5 mentally and financially.

Very accident is occurred due to negligency of rider of the motor cycle, out of this accident crime No.207/2019 is registered before Srinivasapura Police against the said motor cycle and its rider Sudindra.

R1 is owner, R2 is insurer of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners, so that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.30,00,000/.
4.
On service of notice, R1 has appeared through his advocate but not contested the petition by way of filing written statement.

R2/insurer has denied entire case of the petitioners by filing written statement, wherein stated that petitioners have to prove all the allegations made by them, there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) and 134(c) of M.V.Act, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147, 149,
170 of M.V.Act, there is no SCCH 5 neglgiency of rider of the motor cycle, further motor cyclist had no driving license at the time of accident, petitioners have to prove age and income of the deceased,
claim made by them is higher side, hence petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Late. Smt.Vasanthalakshmi died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 02.09.2019 at about 9.00 a.m. near Somayajalapalli Village on Somayajalapalli Ramasamudram Road, Srinivasapura District, due to rash and negligent riding of TVS Apache motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA53EZ7063 by its rider, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH 5 2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has deposed his evidence as PW1 and marked 18 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.18 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:

sentences.text: In order to prove the above issue No.1, petitioner No.1 has deposed his evidence as PW1, wherein he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition, hence in order to avoid the repetition of facts averments made in the affidavit evidence are not reiterated here.

In support of their case, copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of inquest panchanama is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of P.M.Report is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of Charge Sheet is marked as Ex.P.9.
9.
In crossexamination by the counsel for R1 admits that motor cycle was is in slow at the time of SCCH 5 accident which was known road to the rider, due to passing of the dog this accident is occurred.

In cross examination by counsel for R2 admits that, after two days of the incident Arun Kumar has lodged the complaint, motor cycle is damaged on its right side, further taken contention that, this accident is occurred while going on another motor cycle, but said question is denied, they were wearing helmet.

10. On going through the chiefexamination of PW 1 it reveals that, due to negligency of rider of the motor cycle this accident is occurred, but on going through the crossexamination it reveals that, due to passing of the dog rider of the motor cycle has attempted to avoid the accident hence they skid down and sustained injuries.
Ex. P.1 to Ex.P.9 are the police papers.

On going through the same it is noticed that, FIR is against Sudindra and SCCH 5 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA53 EZ7063, deceased Vasanthalakshmi was pillion rider with the said Sudindra, charge sheet speaks that, due to high speed and neglgiency of the Sudindra this accident is occurred, so that, charge sheet is filed against him for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 304A of IPC.
11.

During argument counsel for R2 argued that, very accident is occurred due to passing of the dog,
there is negligency of the motor cyclist.
When there is admission about mistake of the dog and motor cycle was in slow under such circumstances Sec.279 of IPC will not attract, so that, this petition is not maintainable.

On the other hand, counsel for petitioner relied upon charge sheet and submitted that, there is specific recital in the charge sheet marked at Ex.P.9, as such motor cyclists has driven the same in high speed, rash and negligently, SCCH 5 this accident is not occurred due to dashing of the dog, so that, petition is maintainable.
PW1 is not eyewitness in this case, but he has stated that, due to negligency of rider of the motor cycle this accident is occurred.
12. On going through the medical bills marked at Ex.P.18 it is noticed that, treatment is given to the deceased Vasanthalakshmi for cause of the accident.
Further it is noticed that, rider of the motor cycle is not examined by either of the parties.
R1 is the owner of the motor cycle, he has also not contested the petition by way of crossexamination of PW1 and deposing his evidence.

13. Under such circumstances, on the basis of available evidence, this tribunal is of the opinion that,
this accident is not occurred due to the dog, naturally dog was passing on the road, even motor cycle has not SCCH 5 touched the dog, while moving in high speed rash and negligently immediately taken turn of the motor cycle and skid down, admittedly deceased Vasanthalakshmi was moving on Sri. Under such circumstances, this tribunal is of the opinion that, very accident is occurred only due to the negligency of rider of the motor cycle.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:

As per the case of the Petitioners, deceased was aged about 49 years at the time of the accident, in order to prove the said facts, they have produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.10, she is born on 25.09.1970, the alleged accident is occurred on 02.09.2019, hence deceased was aged SCCH 5 about 49 years at the time of accident, hence multiplier 13 is applicable with reference to Sarla Verma case.
15. As per case of the Petitioners, deceased was working as tailor and also homemaker and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m., but to prove the said facts, petitioners have not produced any documents.

Under such circumstances, in the absence of the relevant documentary evidence, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to rely upon Schedule given by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru, so that, notional income of the deceased as per KSLSA Norms for the year 2019 is Rs.14,000/ p.m.

sentences.text:
Hence, this Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.14,000/ p.m.
16.
Petitioner No.1 is the husband, petitioner No.2 and 3 are daughters of the deceased Vasanthalakshmi.
SCCH 5
Under such circumstances, for all the purposes they will become dependents of the deceased.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to 3, then 1/3rd of the income to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/3rd of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 25% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 50 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

(iv) Compensation after Rs.11,667/ x12 Rs.18,20,052/ multiplier of 13 is x 13 applied 19.

Hence, petitioner No.1 being husband of the deceased is entitled for loss of consortium of SCCH 5 Rs.40,000/, further petitioner No.2 & 3 being the daughters of he deceased are entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/ each for loss of parental consortium, further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/ and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/.

Further they have produced medical bills amounting to Rs.1,25,349/ which are marked as Ex.P.18.
20.

The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 18,20,05200 2. Loss of consortium 40,00000 (Petitioner No.1)
3. Loss of parental 80,00000 consortium to petitioner (Rs.40,000/ each)
4. Loss of Estate 15,00000 SCCH 5 5.
Funeral Expenses 15,00000 6.
Medical Bills 1,25,34900 Total 20,95,40100 21.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.20,95,401/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization,
22.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.7012500201188020449000013, which is valid for the period from 10.12.2018 to 09.12.2019, the alleged accident was occurred on 02.09.2019, it reveals that, as on the date of accident insurance policy was in force.
There is no charge sheet against rider of the motor cycle by name Sudindra for the offences punishable under Sec.3 R/w. Sec.181 of M.V.Act.
hence naturally liability SCCH 5 shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

Inview of the above reasoning and discussions to the above issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

SCCH 5 The Respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
